sections.content:
In Spanish, two pronouns starting with 'L' cannot stand side-by-side. When the indirect pronoun 'le' or 'les' is immediately followed by 'lo', 'la', 'los', or 'las', the indirect pronoun changes to 'se':

• le lo → SE LO
• le la → SE LA
• les los → SE LOS
• les las → SE LAS

sections.title: Examples of the le→se Rule
rows: Sí, se lo di. (Not: 'le lo di')
Sí, se la mandé. (Not: 'le la mandé')
Sí, se los presté. (Not: 'les los presté')

items.spanish: Quería decírselo a Carlos, pero se me olvidó.
items.english: I wanted to tell it to Carlos, but I forgot.

items.spanish: El camarero se lo sirvió de inmediato.
items.english: The waiter served it to them right away.

sections.content: Because 'se' can mean 'to him', 'to her', 'to you', or 'to them', you can add 'a él', 'a ella', or 'a ustedes' at the end if clarification is needed: 'Se lo di a ella'.
